extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and workgroup managers (Class 705) and stakeholders in business-method patent examination
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for examining patent applications in automated financial/management/business data processing (USPTO Class 705), including examiner qualifications, training, searching (patent and non-patent literature), and quality-control initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 705 subject-matter definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 705 encompasses machines and their corresponding methods for performing data processing or calculation operations, where the machine or method is utilized in the (1) practice, administration, or management of an enterprise, or (2) processing of financial data, or (3) determination of the charge for goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In lay terms Class 705 covers 20+ financial and management data processing areas (insurance, trading, reservation systems, electronic shopping, auction systems, advertising management, credit/loan processing, point-of-sale, billing, funds transfer, banking, tax processing, HR, scheduling, accounting, inventory monitoring, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical foundation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 705 applications still strongly reflect the implementing electrical and computer engineering that underlies many inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong electrical and computer engineering foundation (databases, communication systems, circuits) is as important as business knowledge for examiners; understanding of non-business fields is required to fully understand many inventions in this class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business-industry experience for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: As Class 705 transitions to being more business-function focused, examiners with business industry work experience are increasingly necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO is increasing examiner training and hiring to add examiners with ≥3 years of relevant business experience (banking, securities, marketing analysis, insurance, business information systems, financial analysis, etc.). Business experience aids examination of business-function-focused applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary vs Non-Primary examiner roles and signatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary Examiners and managers are delegated signatory authority to grant patents; non-Primary examiners are apprentices whose work must be reviewed and signed by a person with signatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent examining is a master-apprentice profession learned on-the-job with primary examiners acting as masters and reviewers of non-primary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource/hiring strategy and focus on quality during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Workgroup 2760 will hire sufficient Class 705 examiners to cover attrition and modest expansion, with FY2000 focusing on maintaining high quality during the transition toward business-method claim formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expansion is calibrated; quality efforts are resource intensive and the results depend on available examiner hiring and training resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner profile balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an appropriate balance of electrical engineering, computer science, and business knowledge among Class 705 examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO adjusts mix of training and experience (MBAs, JDs, PhDs, Masters) to keep examiner knowledge aligned with the content of business data processing inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid Examiner-Trainer role
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Examiner-Trainers — Primary Examiners that spend 50% of time examining and 50% training others to promote consistent examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New examiners work closely with Examiner-Trainers to learn legal, procedural, and technological aspects; Examiner-Trainers facilitate integration of new hires and consistent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural training curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: All examiners receive staged legal, procedural and technical training: initial two-week intensive patent-procedure training, followed by on-the-job orientation, two-week Introduction to Practice and Procedure (IPP) after ~2 months, then weekly advanced practice & procedure courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include statutes (35 U.S.C.), rules (37 C.F.R.), affidavit practice, PCT procedures, 35 U.S.C. 101 training, and orientation to USPTO electronic systems for searching and tracking workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workgroup 2760 training manual standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A training manual (100+ pages) focusing on analyzing the specification and claims, searching, and preparing written reports (office actions) is used to bring new examiners up to speed within ~6 months and to ensure consistent examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual contains samples of actions, guidance on handling/responding to amendments, and is distributed to new examiners immediately; used in apprentice training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search-strategy training and standardized base strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers and Primary Examiners have formulated standardized base search strategies for varying aspects of the business technology to guide examiners where and how to search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A search strategy advisory panel (managers + experienced examiners) assists examiners in developing search strategies and may provide legal/procedural assistance; while each application is unique, standardized strategies steer searches in patent and commercial databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory search requirements for Class 705
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must perform a mandatory search for all Class 705 applications including a classified U.S. patent document search and a text search of U.S. patent documents, foreign patent documents, and non-patent literature (NPL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPL searches include required search areas mapped/correlated to the U.S. classification system for Class 705; e.g., for a 705/4 insurance application the examiner must search the 22 mandatory general business databases plus 3 mandatory insurance-specific databases (see core database lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core non-patent literature (NPL) databases requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All Class 705 applications will be searched in a specified set of core NPL databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure NPL-1 lists core databases that must be searched (examples include: ABI/INFORM, Business & Industry, Business Week, Business Wire, Computer Database, Conference Papers Index, Dissertation Abstracts Online, Globalbase, INSPEC, Internet & Personal Computing Abstracts, McGraw-Hill Publications Online, Microcomputer Software Guide Online, NPA/Plus, Newsletter Database, Newspapers, Financial Times Abstracts, New York Times Abstracts, Wall Street Journal Abstracts, PR Newswire, PROMT, Softbase, Trade & Industry Database, Wilson Applied Science & Technology Abstracts, World Reporter). Examiners must also search appropriate databases among ~900 available commercial databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-specific core databases per subclass
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the general core databases, subject-specific core databases exist for particular Class 705 subclasses and must be searched for applications classified under those subclasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are required to search these subclass-specific databases (the white paper defines mandatory lists per subclass; e.g., insurance-specific databases for 705/4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial database training and usage (DIALOG, STN/CAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 705 examiners receive training in commercial NPL providers (DIALOG, STN/CAS) in two parts: orientation to the database and hands-on exercises with real-world examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is provided by the Patent Academy and the workgroup; if examiners prefer, they can request EIC to perform commercial database searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of STIC / Electronic Information Center (EIC) support
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC-EIC provides search and library support for Class 705 examiners, including non-patent literature searches and retrieval of hard copies of NPL documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EIC staff perform professional searches (expanded staff from 2 in 1995 to 12 in FY2000), collect business literature, and produce a daily e-mail with new/interesting business information (including web sites); STIC is developing a web-based tool collating examining resources for Class 705.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patent literature reliance guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: For rapidly emerging technologies and simple accounting procedures, the U.S. patent database may be less valuable and examiners will rely on NPL to provide relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPL covers textbooks, newspaper/magazine articles, sales brochures, professional journals, conference proceedings, and web sites; examiners must integrate NPL into searches and examination where patent literature is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality-improvement initiatives and review measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous quality initiatives include Examiner-Trainers, enhanced training, search improvements, March 2000 initiatives for additional review, and in-process review mechanisms to ensure high-quality examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO's mission is to help customers get patents but examiners must apply statute and rules (35 U.S.C., 37 C.F.R.); examiners must analyze claims, determine if burden of proof for denial is met, and may point out patentable inventions disclosed but unclaimed. Quality initiatives are resource intensive and are continuously updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to assist applicants and analyze claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent examiner is tasked with helping the inventor, including pointing out patentable inventions disclosed but not claimed, and with analyzing the scope of claims to determine whether sufficient evidence exists to meet the burden of proof to deny patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent statute presumes entitlement to a patent unless the examiner meets the burden of proof to deny; examiners must balance assistance with proper application of legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of USPTO patent search systems (EAST/WEST) and internal tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are trained to search U.S. patent databases (EAST and WEST) and to use USPTO electronic systems for searching, preparing actions, and tracking workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial training covers how these systems operate; combined patent-database and commercial-NPL searching is required for Class 705.
